findings.claim: The rollback note in the component page does not name the dump object, and the only way back to 2.0.0 is an object anyone can overwrite or lose. backup-postgres writes pgdumpall-$(date +%Y-%m-%d).sql.gz and rclone copy overwrites it, so any other run of the job on UTC date 2026-10-20 replaces the 2.0.0 dump with a 2.3.1 one (the bucket has no versioning). The bucket's 180-day lifecycle rule deletes it after that. The path is recorded only in .loop/spikes/bifrost-update/5. Name gs://localstack-cluster-backups/postgres/pgdumpall-2026-10-20.sql.gz in the page and say it is a pg_dumpall of the whole cluster, kept 180 days, and overwritten by another backup-postgres run on that UTC date. Or copy it to a name no job writes and give that name.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
The pin is 2.3.1, the provider stays at ~>0.1.0, the smoke probe expects `access_not_found`, and the component page records the version and the migration that cannot be undone.
The live job runs v2.3.1 and is healthy, and I confirmed the post-switch traffic on my own.
One docs finding that does not block: the page points readers at the rollback dump without naming it, and that dump can be overwritten or expire.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree passed pre_commit, cli_tests and eval-row r1, with "stamp green: d91b88a1...".
That fingerprint matches the one spike 5's run.json recorded, so the live evidence ran on this tree.
Code read in full: the staged diff of services.tf, bifrost_smoke.py, cli/tests/test_bifrost_version.py and .okf/components/bifrost.md.
`bifrost_version` feeds only `image = docker.io/maximhq/bifrost:v${bifrost_version}` in bifrost.hcl:40.
The smoke probe's label is compared against the response `type`, so the rename is the only change it needs.
r1: the test's regex finds every `bifrost_version = "..."` and asserts it equals exactly ["2.3.1"], so another version or "latest" fails it.
It asserts the `~>0.1.0` string inside the `bifrost = {}` block of providers.tf, and it asserts that the smoke tuple has `access_not_found` and no `virtual_key_not_found`.
Each fails_when clause is asserted.

r2 (judgment): spike 5 records a forced backup-postgres run at 10:24:51 UTC writing gs://localstack-cluster-backups/postgres/pgdumpall-2026-10-20.sql.gz before the job was submitted at 10:25:55 UTC (nomad job status).
The backup-postgres.hcl command is pg_dumpall, so it covers the `bifrost` database.
Met.
f1 covers how long that dump stays usable.
r3 (judgment): `nomad job status bifrost` shows deployment e457904c successful, one healthy alloc on version 11.

Spike 5's stdout has the smoke script passing all five checks on v2.3.1, a bare-string rerank through the OpenViking key returning 200 with the correct order, and a second plan reporting "No changes".

Spike 5's Prometheus query used a 10m window that started before the switch, so I queried again myself: process_start_time is 10:26:10 UTC, and the new process's counters show bifrost_success_requests_total from openviking (embedding 3, rerank 2) and hermes (embedding 2) to embark.
`sum(increase(...[3m]))`, a window that falls wholly after the start, gives 4.8 success and 7.2 upstream.
These are the series the dashboard's `sum(rate(...[5m]))` panels read.
`up` is 1.
Met.
r4 (judgment): the component page names v2.3.1 as the image and has a version-history paragraph on the migration that cannot be undone.
A grep of docs/, README.md and .okf/ for a Bifrost 2.0.0 claim found none still naming it as current.
The ">= 2.0.0"-style mentions in ADR 0008 and bifrost.hcl are historical or still true.
Met.
The missing baseline run on 2.0.0: once the label rename is in, the new script fails on 2.0.0 by design, so a before-run would have needed the old script.
The baseline guards against an after-run that passes only because the property never held.
Every assertion passed after the switch.
Spike 4 showed keys made on 2.0.0 survive, and spike 3 showed bare-string rerank works on both versions.
I accept the gap.
f1 (docs, not blocking): the bifrost.md rollback paragraph says the way back is "the backup-postgres dump taken just before the apply" but does not name it.
The object name has only a date in it, rclone overwrites it, and the bucket deletes objects after 180 days with no versioning.
Name the object and its limits, or copy it to a name no job writes.
The plan says 2.3.0 adds an `app` label on request metrics.
The live series carry no `app` label.
That does not matter here, because the dashboard sums every label away.
